title: Strong Nash equilibria
description: A profile of a graphical game is a strong Nash equilibrium if no coalition can change its members' actions so that every member gains; deciding whether one exists is Sigma-2-complete (Gottlob, Greco and Scarcello). The abstraction guesses a profile and the check a coalition with a joint deviation, which depends only on the actions of the members and of their neighbours. The sample game has 5 Nash equilibria, 1 of them strong.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The players, their neighbours and their payoffs. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.
% player(P), action(A), w(P,Q,W) and bonus(P,A,B), as explained there.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): one action per player.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a profile, that is, one action for every player.
1 { act(P,A) : action(A) } 1 :- player(P).
#show act/2.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the players' actions.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a coalition whose members all gain by a joint deviation (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: a coalition s/1 and a new profile new/2 in which only members of
% the coalition act differently (a member may also keep its action) ...
1 { s(P) : player(P) }.
1 { new(P,A) : action(A) } 1 :- player(P).
:- new(P,A), not s(P), not act(P,A).
% ... and every member is strictly better off. A player's payoff is the sum of w over
% the neighbours with the same action, plus the bonus of its action.
:- s(P), #sum {  W,Q : w(P,Q,W), new(P,A), new(Q,A) ;  B,bonus : new(P,A), bonus(P,A,B) ;
                -W,Q : w(P,Q,W), act(P,A), act(Q,A) ; -B,bonus : act(P,A), bonus(P,A,B) } <= 0.
#show s/1.
#show to(P,A) : s(P), new(P,A).

% The members' old and new payoffs depend on the actions of the members and of their
% neighbours, and on nothing else.
near(P) :- s(P).
near(Q) :- s(P), w(P,Q,_).
relevant(act(P,A)) :- near(P), act(P,A).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts:
% A graphical game: eight players, each chooses action 1 or 2.
player(1..8).
action(1..2).
% w(P,Q,W): player P gets W for choosing the same action as neighbour Q (W may be
% negative: P would rather differ from Q). Players only care about their neighbours.
w(1,2,-1). w(1,5,2). w(1,8,-1).
w(2,1,2). w(2,3,1).
w(3,2,3). w(3,4,2). w(3,5,1). w(3,6,1).
w(4,3,3). w(4,5,-2).
w(5,1,3). w(5,3,2). w(5,4,1). w(5,6,2).
w(6,3,-2). w(6,5,2). w(6,7,3).
w(7,6,-1). w(7,8,3).
w(8,1,-1). w(8,7,-1).
% bonus(P,A,B): player P gets B on top for choosing action A.
bonus(1,1,0). bonus(1,2,0).
bonus(2,1,1). bonus(2,2,0).
bonus(3,1,0). bonus(3,2,1).
bonus(4,1,0). bonus(4,2,2).
bonus(5,1,2). bonus(5,2,1).
bonus(6,1,1). bonus(6,2,1).
bonus(7,1,2). bonus(7,2,0).
bonus(8,1,2). bonus(8,2,2).

% Three players who all want to choose the same action: both unanimous
% profiles are strong equilibria.
player(1..3).
action(1..2).
w(P,Q,1) :- player(P), player(Q), P != Q.
bonus(P,A,0) :- player(P), action(A).

% Player 1 wants to match player 2, player 2 wants to differ: there is no
% equilibrium at all.
player(1..2).
action(1..2).
w(1,2,1). w(2,1,-1).
bonus(P,A,0) :- player(P), action(A).

% Five players: the game has two Nash equilibria, but a coalition can improve
% on each of them, so there is no strong one.
player(1..5).
action(1..2).
w(1,2,2). w(1,4,2). w(2,3,-2). w(2,4,-2). w(3,1,3). w(3,5,-1).
w(4,1,3). w(4,2,2). w(5,3,-1). w(5,4,1).
bonus(3,1,1). bonus(3,2,2). bonus(4,2,1). bonus(5,1,1). bonus(5,2,2).

generators.name: graphical
generators.description: A random graphical game with two actions: players P < Q are neighbours with probability p/1000, each direction with its own weight in -3..3; each action has a bonus in 0..2.
generators.text:
% graphical: n players, actions 1 and 2; neighbours with probability p/1000.
player(1..n).
action(1..2).
nb(P,Q) :- player(P), player(Q), P < Q, @flip(p, P, Q, nb) = 1.
w(P,Q,@int(-3, 3, P, Q, w)) :- nb(P,Q).
w(Q,P,@int(-3, 3, Q, P, w)) :- nb(P,Q).
bonus(P,A,@int(0, 2, P, A, bonus)) :- player(P), action(A).
#show player/1.  #show action/1.  #show w/3.  #show bonus/3.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 5):
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + abstraction   options "--enum-mode=record"
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

readme:
# Project: strong Nash equilibria

## Research question

Deciding whether a strong Nash equilibrium exists is Σ2P-complete. Which refinement (the coalition, its members' actions, the neighbourhood) cuts the most candidates?

## Baseline

1 solution (exhausted) after 70 candidates and 69 clauses (0.1 s) on the example.

## Things to try

- Variants with the three refinements and a campaign over the instances.
- A generator of random graphical games and a scaling plot.
- A loop with two checks: Nash first (cheap), then coalitions (see `lang-two-stage`).

## How to measure

Add the variants, write a suite over the instances (Campaign tab, Advanced mode), and read the instance × variant matrix; headless: `node tools/bench.mjs <id> --suite NAME --out rows.jsonl` and `node tools/report.mjs rows.jsonl`. Check every variant against the `reference` loop (or the audit) on small instances before trusting its numbers.

spaces.description: Coordination games with size players and two actions.
spaces.text:
% every coordination game: players 1..size, two actions, weights 0 or 1, bonuses 0 or 1
player(1..size).  action(1..2).
{ w(P,Q,1) : player(P), player(Q), P != Q }.
1 { bonus(P,A,B) : B = 0..1 } 1 :- player(P), action(A).
